blocks.text: These two relationships are intentionally different. Converting both members to pointers would not automatically improve flexibility; it could conceal which one owns its target. The member declarations should help a reviewer draw the lifetime graph before reading the function bodies.

blocks.text: Composition puts smaller objects inside a larger object or connects them through explicit references and owners. A reporter can own a formatter as a value because it needs an independent formatting configuration. It can borrow a sink when the caller controls a destination that outlives the reporter. It could instead own a unique sink if the reporter itself should control that destination’s lifetime. Those are separate interface choices.

blocks.text: A has-a relationship does not automatically mean dynamic allocation. A member value has its lifetime tied to the enclosing object and can often avoid an extra allocation or indirection. Use a pointer when optionality, polymorphic identity, transfer, or a separate lifetime actually requires one. The smallest adequate ownership model is often easier to inspect than a graph of heap allocations created by habit.

blocks.text: Member declaration order becomes a design tool when components depend on one another. If a member borrows another member during its lifetime, arrange construction and destruction so the owner exists before the borrower is constructed and remains alive until after the borrower is destroyed. Better still, avoid persistent internal borrows when a call-time reference can express the relationship more simply.

blocks.text: Copying a composed object follows the semantics of each member. Copying the reporter copies its formatter value but preserves the reference member’s observation of the same sink. That can be intentional, but it is not an independent copy of the destination. A class containing references may also have implicitly deleted assignment operations. Review these consequences before describing the reporter as a freely copyable value.

topics.summary: The reporter’s sample operation asks the formatter to create text and then asks the sink to write it. It does not duplicate numeric formatting or inspect a sink’s concrete storage. Delegation keeps the coordinating function small while the actual responsibilities remain visible.

blocks.text: A failed formatting or sink operation can propagate through this simple interface. A production version should specify retry, partial-output, and error-reporting semantics according to the destination. Do not add blanket exception swallowing merely to make a void interface appear infallible. Small interfaces still need honest failure contracts.
rich: A failed formatting or sink operation can propagate through this simple interface. A production version should specify retry, partial-output, and error-reporting semantics according to the destination. Do not add blanket exception swallowing merely to make a void interface appear infallible. Small interfaces still need honest failure contracts.

blocks.text: Delegation means giving a collaborator a well-defined part of the work. The reporter asks the formatter for a string and then asks the sink to write it. The formatter does not choose the destination, and the sink does not decide how a sample should be represented. This division makes each component’s behavior smaller and gives tests a clear place to observe results.

blocks.text: Do not split a function into objects merely to maximize the number of classes. A useful boundary corresponds to an independent policy, dependency, or invariant. A formatting rule that changes separately from a destination is a reasonable boundary. A wrapper with one method that merely forwards an integer to another wrapper may add indirection without providing a meaningful contract.

A formatting rule that changes separately from a destination is a reasonable boundary. blocks.text: Delegation also determines failure boundaries. If formatting throws before the sink is called, no write should occur through this reporter invocation. If the sink fails after partially publishing text, the reporter cannot undo the destination’s external state simply by catching the exception. It may report failure, retry under an explicit idempotency policy, or use a different destination protocol. The local object model does not automatically supply an external transaction.

It is not intended to model every failure mode of a terminal, file, network socket, or database. Use a fake for the contract being exercised and a separate integration test for real external behavior.

blocks.text: The in-memory sink is a fake with simple real behavior, not a guarantee that every external adapter behaves identically under failure. Tests can verify the reporter’s contract quickly, while integration tests must verify actual file or network boundaries separately. Substitution helps isolation; it does not eliminate the need to test real dependencies.

blocks.text: Programming against an abstraction means that the caller depends on the required behavior, not on one concrete implementation’s representation. The sink interface exposes writing a string. A reporter should not downcast the sink to a memory sink to inspect its vector during ordinary operation. The test can own a concrete memory sink and inspect its results from outside the reporter while the reporter itself remains decoupled.

blocks.text: Interface-based design works at compile time too. A template parameter can require a suitable callable or sink operation without a virtual base. Runtime polymorphism is useful when implementations are selected and stored through a stable runtime interface. Templates are useful when concrete types are known at instantiation and static composition fits the program. Neither mechanism is universally more modern than the other.

The interface should say whether a successful return means the text was accepted, buffered, or durably stored. Those are increasingly strong claims. A memory sink can support acceptance into its vector; it does not establish durability.

topics.title: 10.2.2 Replacing Inheritance with Composition
topics.summary: Replacing inheritance with composition removes the false is-a relationship. The reporter no longer inherits unrelated destination methods or relies on protected destination state. Its constructor states exactly which components it requires.

cards.question: Explain Replacing Inheritance with Composition in your own words.
cards.answer: Replacing inheritance with composition removes the false is-a relationship. The reporter no longer inherits unrelated destination methods or relies on protected destination state. Its constructor states exactly which components it requires.

blocks.text: Replacing inheritance with composition removes the false is-a relationship. The reporter no longer inherits unrelated destination methods or relies on protected destination state. Its constructor states exactly which components it requires.

blocks.text: Composition also makes ownership choices explicit. A borrowed sink is suitable when an enclosing scope manages several reporters and the destination. An exclusively owned sink may be appropriate when the reporter must determine its lifetime. A shared sink owner is appropriate only when several independent owners genuinely participate in lifetime. Select among those policies deliberately rather than treating one smart-pointer type as a universal interface.
rich: Composition also makes ownership choices explicit. A borrowed sink is suitable when an enclosing scope manages several reporters and the destination. An exclusively owned sink may be appropriate when the reporter must determine its lifetime. A shared sink owner is appropriate only when several independent owners genuinely participate in lifetime. Select among those policies deliberately rather than treating one smart-pointer type as a universal interface.

blocks.text: Inheritance is often overused when the real goal is policy reuse. A reporter derived from a formatter exposes a type relationship that callers probably do not need. A reporter containing a formatter says exactly what is needed and can delegate formatting without inheriting unrelated operations. Changing the formatter’s internal data does not automatically change the reporter’s base-class representation contract.

blocks.text: Composition also permits independent replacement. The same reporter can use a different formatter value and a different sink implementation without creating a new subclass for every combination. A hierarchy with subclasses for “CSV-to-file,” “CSV-to-memory,” “text-to-file,” and “text-to-memory” multiplies classes when two independent choices would be clearer.

blocks.text: Do not replace all inheritance mechanically. A well-defined runtime interface with genuine substitutable implementations can be an excellent design, as Chapter 9 showed. The aim is to avoid encoding every reuse relationship as public inheritance. Ask which relationship the application actually needs: value containment, temporary borrowing, exclusive ownership, shared lifetime, or runtime substitution.

blocks.text: When refactoring an existing hierarchy into composition, preserve behavior with tests at the public boundary. Keep expected output, failure reporting, and lifetime semantics stable unless the change intentionally revises the contract. A design improvement that silently drops errors or retains borrowed objects longer is not merely an internal cleanup.

reading.title: 10.2.2 Replacing Inheritance with Composition
paragraphs: Replacing inheritance with composition removes the false is-a relationship. The reporter no longer inherits unrelated destination methods or relies on protected destination state. Its constructor states exactly which components it requires.

Composition also makes ownership choices explicit. A borrowed sink is suitable when an enclosing scope manages several reporters and the destination. An exclusively owned sink may be appropriate when the reporter must determine its lifetime. A shared sink owner is appropriate only when several independent owners genuinely participate in lifetime. Select among those policies deliberately rather than treating one smart-pointer type as a universal interface.

Inheritance is often overused when the real goal is policy reuse. A reporter derived from a formatter exposes a type relationship that callers probably do not need. A reporter containing a formatter says exactly what is needed and can delegate formatting without inheriting unrelated operations. Changing the formatter’s internal data does not automatically change the reporter’s base-class representation contract.

Composition also permits independent replacement. The same reporter can use a different formatter value and a different sink implementation without creating a new subclass for every combination. A hierarchy with subclasses for “CSV-to-file,” “CSV-to-memory,” “text-to-file,” and “text-to-memory” multiplies classes when two independent choices would be clearer.

Do not replace all inheritance mechanically. A well-defined runtime interface with genuine substitutable implementations can be an excellent design, as Chapter 9 showed. The aim is to avoid encoding every reuse relationship as public inheritance. Ask which relationship the application actually needs: value containment, temporary borrowing, exclusive ownership, shared lifetime, or runtime substitution.

When refactoring an existing hierarchy into composition, preserve behavior with tests at the public boundary. Keep expected output, failure reporting, and lifetime semantics stable unless the change intentionally revises the contract. A design improvement that silently drops errors or retains borrowed objects longer is not merely an internal cleanup.

topics.title: Failure clinic — A borrowed sink escaped its owner
topics.summary: A helper creates a local memory sink, constructs a reporter that references it, and returns the reporter. The reporter’s formatter survives by value, but its sink reference dangles as soon as the helper returns. Copying or moving the reporter does not extend the sink’s lifetime. The repair is to move destination ownership into the returned object, return both components in a lifetime-safe arrangement, or require a caller-owned sink that lives long enough.
